content.comment_body: I'm just starting out with PLC programming. I have a scenario where the [product_name] 230 RC would be ideal, but I'm unsure how to initiate the program automatically when machine power is switched on, and then utilize the programmed timer after a switch is activated.
The memory location M8 (startup flag) behaves differently. M8 is only active in the first cycle. You can use M8, for example, to set a reset/set function or to implement an off delay.

analysis.insight_summary: A user new to PLC programming struggles with how to start a process automatically at machine power-up and trigger a timer via a switch. Experienced members explain that some memory flags built into the PLC, such as special startup cycles, can be used for this function, while also noting the lack of clear standard instructions for newcomers.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for clear, straightforward directions or conventional programming strategies for starting machine operation at power-up and employing a timer based on a switch input.
pain_keywords: lack of clear startup programming instructions
